overview: Mexico draws more international visitors than almost anywhere else in the Americas, and the range is part of the appeal — colonial cities with centuries of layered history, Caribbean and Pacific coastlines, desert and jungle, all within a few hours of each other.

For most Western passport holders, entry is refreshingly simple: no advance visa application, just a valid passport and the standard tourist paperwork issued on arrival. That simplicity is exactly why it remains one of the most-visited countries in the world year after year.

attractions.name: Chichén Itzá
attractions.description: One of the New Seven Wonders of the World, and the most visited archaeological site in Mexico.

attractions.name: Tulum
attractions.description: Maya ruins perched directly above Caribbean beaches, unlike anywhere else in the region.

attractions.name: Mexico City Zócalo & Templo Mayor
attractions.description: The historic heart of the capital, built atop the ruins of the Aztec empire's main temple.

attractions.name: Teotihuacán
attractions.description: Ancient pyramid city just outside Mexico City, home to the Pyramid of the Sun.

attractions.name: Playa del Carmen
attractions.description: A laid-back base for exploring the Riviera Maya's beaches and cenotes.

overview: France is consistently the most-visited country on Earth by international arrivals, and Paris alone accounts for only part of the draw — the French Riviera, the châteaux of the Loire Valley, and the wine regions of Bordeaux and Burgundy all pull their own steady stream of travelers.

As part of the Schengen Area, France's entry rules are shared with 26 other European countries — a single visa-free allowance covers short stays across the whole zone, not just France, which is worth knowing if a trip spans multiple countries.

attractions.name: Eiffel Tower
attractions.description: The most-visited paid monument in the world, and the defining symbol of Paris.

attractions.name: Louvre Museum
attractions.description: The world's most-visited museum, and home to the Mona Lisa.

attractions.name: Palace of Versailles
attractions.description: The opulent former royal residence just outside Paris, with gardens stretching over 800 hectares.

attractions.name: Notre-Dame Cathedral
attractions.description: A masterpiece of French Gothic architecture, still one of the most iconic sights on the Seine.

attractions.name: French Riviera
attractions.description: The glamorous Mediterranean coastline stretching from Cannes to Menton.
